SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY — MOCK EXAM #6
====

GRADE: Grade 6
SUBJECT: SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours
TOTAL MARKS: 80
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Invertebrates? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Invertebrates.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Invertebrates.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Invertebrates.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Invertebrates.

2. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Heating until a solid melts
   B. Movement of water only across a membrane
   C. A chemical reaction forming ash
   D. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

3. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 0 °C
   B. 50 °C
   C. 100 °C
   D. 37 °C

4. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Ice melting to water
   B. Paper burning to ash
   C. Iron rusting
   D. Milk souring

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Composition of Air? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Composition of Air.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Composition of Air.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Composition of Air.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Composition of Air.

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Levers as simple machines? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Levers as simple machines.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Levers as simple machines.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Levers as simple machines.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Levers as simple machines.

7. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water always increases oxygen
   B. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   C. Petrol fires have no fuel
   D. Water removes heat too quickly

8. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Primary consumers only
   B. Tertiary consumers
   C. Decomposers only
   D. Producers

9. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. newton (N)
   B. joule (J)
   C. watt (W)
   D. pascal (Pa)

10. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   B. Overgrazing continuously
   C. Burning crop residue every week
   D. Removing all vegetation

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Light? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Light.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Light.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Light.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Light.

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Slopes as simple machines? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Slopes as simple machines.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Slopes as simple machines.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Slopes as simple machines.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Slopes as simple machines.

13. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   B. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   C. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   D. A compound can be separated by filtering only

14. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. A mixture of two liquids
   B. Any white crystal used in cooking
   C. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   D. Any substance that conducts electricity

15. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only carbon dioxide
   B. Nitrogen gas only
   C. Only water vapour
   D. Glucose and oxygen

16. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Change of State? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Change of State.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Change of State.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Change of State.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Change of State.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
17. In three clear sentences, explain Light and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Levers as simple machines and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Slopes as simple machines and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Invertebrates and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Change of State and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain Composition of Air and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

23. In three clear sentences, explain Light and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

24. In three clear sentences, explain Levers as simple machines and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
